title: Clitoria ternatea (Butterfly Pea) – Health Benefits, Uses & How to Make Tea
seoTitle: Butterfly Pea Tea Benefits and How to Make It
excerpt: Discover butterfly pea tea benefits, from antioxidants to natural colour, plus a simple recipe, safety notes and how this herbal tea tastes.
content:
What Is Clitoria ternatea (Butterfly Pea)?

Clitoria ternatea, commonly known as butterfly pea or Asian pigeonwings, is a tropical flowering plant prized for its vivid blue blooms and traditional wellness uses. The flowers contain natural pigments called ternatins, which give them their striking color and are packed with antioxidant compounds. People have used butterfly pea in Ayurvedic medicine for centuries to support memory, relaxation, and overall well-being. Today, it is also popular as a caffeine-free herbal tea and a natural food coloring for rice, desserts, and drinks.

What Are the Health Benefits of Butterfly Pea?

Butterfly pea flowers are rich in anthocyanins and flavonoids, plant compounds studied for their antioxidant effects. Research published in 2025–2026 suggests these compounds may help protect cells against oxidative stress, support memory and cognitive function, and reduce anxiety. The flower is also being investigated for skin health, anti-inflammatory effects, and eye health support. Traditional Ayurvedic medicine uses butterfly pea preparations for memory support, relaxation, and general wellness, though these uses are not yet confirmed by clinical trials.

How to Make Butterfly Pea Tea at Home

  1. Rinse 5–10 fresh butterfly pea flowers (or 1 tsp dried) under clean water.
  2. Place the flowers in a cup and pour 250 ml of hot water (not boiling) over them.
  3. Steep for 5–10 minutes until the water turns a vibrant blue.
  4. Strain the flowers and enjoy the caffeine-free herbal tea.
  5. Add a squeeze of lemon juice to watch the color change from blue to purple.

Using Butterfly Pea as Natural Food Colouring

Butterfly pea flowers produce a natural blue pigment called ternatin, which makes them an excellent plant-based food coloring. To use, soak fresh or dried flowers in hot water for 15–20 minutes, strain the liquid, and use the blue infusion to color rice, desserts, drinks, and baked goods. Adding lemon juice shifts the color from blue to purple, offering a natural, dye-free alternative to synthetic food colors.

Safety & Precautions When Using Butterfly Pea

Use only pesticide-free, correctly identified flowers. Pregnant or breastfeeding women and people taking blood-pressure or blood-sugar medication should consult a healthcare professional before using butterfly pea. Do not use as a replacement for prescribed medicines. Discontinue use if you experience allergic reactions or digestive discomfort.

Is butterfly pea tea safe to drink every day?

Yes, butterfly pea tea is generally safe for daily consumption in moderate amounts (1–2 cups). It is caffeine-free and rich in antioxidants. However, pregnant or breastfeeding women and people on medication should consult a doctor first.

Why does butterfly pea tea change color with lemon?

Butterfly pea tea contains anthocyanins, which are pH-sensitive pigments. The tea is naturally blue because the flower infusion is slightly alkaline. Adding acidic lemon juice lowers the pH, causing the color to shift from blue to purple — a natural, dye-free color change.

Where can I buy butterfly pea flowers?

You can find butterfly pea flowers at Indian grocery stores, nurseries, or online herb and spice retailers. Look for organic, pesticide-free dried flowers or fresh blooms. You can also grow the climbing vine at home from seeds in a sunny spot with a trellis.
